author: Trapping Value
title: Enbridge ( ENB ) shares have rebounded off the lows but are
text:
Enbridge ( ENB ) shares have rebounded off the lows but are still one of the cheapest ways to get predictable high dividend growth while paying significantly less than a market multiple. 
We recently recommended ENB as the market was throwing a tantrum over its funding plan and prospects for dividend growth. Since then, ENB has clarified its funding and dividend growth prospects over the next 3 years. However the stock still remains in the deep value zone. It is being priced like a commodity stock while functioning like a utility. Extrapolating a market multiple within 3 years gives us prospects for over 100% total returns.
Dividend growth was never a question in our minds While the failure to guide for high dividend growth caused a selloff in 2017, to us there was no doubt that ENB would grow its dividend at least 5-8% a year. ENB confirmed those thoughts with a 10% dividend hike starting with the March 2018 quarter. ENB also gave its range of adjusted cash flow from operations (ACFFO) for 2018-2020.
Source: ENB presentation 
The amounts are in Canadian dollars (CAD). Based on our Fx outlook for USD-CAD, we think this will translate into $4.30 USD (midpoint) of ACFFO. The dividend forecast is a bit harder as although ENB has moved with a 10% increase in range, we think the relative dearth of projects post that time frame could make ENB boost its dividends even faster. As such our base case is for ENB to guide for about $3.50 CAD (about $3.00 USD) in dividends for 2021.
Why our numbers could prove conservative ENB has historically beaten its guidance over the years with 2017 proving to be an exception. Based on the numbers in its December forecast, we think ENB has again set up the stage to beat by using very conservative numbers. There are two other factors that will help swing the numbers further in favor of ENB.
ENB currently has very little commodity price exposure.

However, its ability to set long-term tolls on its infrastructure is definitely impacted by commodity market strength. For new projects that come online in 2020, we expect very strong pricing, as we believe we will likely see very high crude prices in 2019 and 2020. Where ENB has commodity price exposure, this is likely to help rather than hurt as pricing improves materially from 2017 levels.
The other area of material upside surprise will come through market repricing of ENB's risk in our opinion. This will significantly decrease ENB's cost of capital and on both the equity and debt side. ENB still requires funding for its projects and as the stock reprices higher, DRIP funding and other capital raised will come at a significantly lower rate.

A target price We see ENB worthy of at least a market multiple on its ACFFO. Based on our 2020 target, we see that equating to $73 USD a share (17x $4.30 USD). This does not assume any upside from the factors mentioned above. Another way to look at it would be what would the price be if ENB yielded as much as comparable utility-like companies.
D Dividend Yield (TTM) data by YCharts ENB currently yields far more than Dominion Energy ( D ), Exelon ( EXC ) or even the Utilities Select Sector Spider ETF ( XLU ). Just like these utility stocks, ENB has very little commodity price exposure. In fact, at 4% commodity price exposure, we would venture to say it is definitely lower than that of the average utility company. The longer-term chart shows that ENB actually carried a lower dividend yield than all of the 3 comparatives for a majority of the time span. Hence, the significantly higher current yield is an aberration in our view.
D Dividend Yield (TTM) data by YCharts A $3.00 USD dividend with a 4% dividend yield gets us to a $75 target. With reinvested dividends this comes to a total return of over 100% in 3 years and an 8% plus ending yield on cost.
Risk factors The biggest risk comes from execution and approval risk on the line 3 replacement program . As far as the debt metrics are concerned, ENB has them well under control.
In fact, in this part of the cycle, we would have preferred if ENB used more leverage and did not issue the stock it recently did. Unlike the rating agencies, we don't see much cause for concern but that might be because we are bullish on energy and see any residual counterparty risk fading away over the next year or two.
Conclusion ENB is designed to deliver pretty fantastic returns for growth investors. This comes as a direct result of the current low valuation and the market penchant for chasing technology stocks. On our scale of 1-10, where 1 would be "Avoid like the bubonic plague" and 10 would be "Buy like this is Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) in March 2009," we would rate ENB a STRONG BUY and at 7.5. 
Disclaimer: Please note that this is not financial advice. It may seem like, sound like it, but it is not. Investors are expected to do their own due diligence and consult with a professional who knows their objectives and constraints. ENB is dual listed on NYSE and TSX. ENB dividends are qualified dividends but will have taxes withheld outside of sheltered accounts for US investors.
